newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut bank shares up on week.
newsitem.headline: Beirut bank shares up on week.

text.p: Bank shares made gains on the Beirut Stock Exchange in the week ended on Friday. Brokers expected more gains next week but said Solidere was expected to outperform the market.
The LIBX bank index rose 4.86 percent on the week to 171.78. The LISPI general index rose 1.41 percent to 90.70 and the BLOM general index rose 0.40 percent to 968.66.
Market turnover was 928,235 shares from 895,941 and value was $10,237,265 against $9,091,750.
Solidere A and B shares were mixed in heavy demand.
A shares fell to $10.875 from $11 while B shares rose to $11.25 from $11 on June 24 when they went ex-dividend after shareholders approved a 25 cents dividend on Monday -- 25 percent up on last year.

"I think Solidere will be the star next week," Georges Abou Jaoude of Beirut finance house Financial Funds Advisors told Reuters. "We are very positive on Solidere...I think the stock will outperform the market next week."
Banque Audi, considered by many brokers the market's blue chip, ended at $26.25 from $25.375 a week earlier after touching a record $27 during the week.
"Audi is expected to stabilise around today's level but its longterm trend is believed to be upwards," a broker said.
Banque Libanaise pour Le Commerce hit a new high of $20 from $19.625 and its Global Depositary Receipts traded at $22.9-$23.35 in London. "The share is still the cheapest in Beirut," a broker said.

Bank of Beirut rose to a new high of $4.375 from $4.0. The bank reported on July 3 a 72.5 percent increase in mid-year profits to $4.096 million and brokers said the results met top maket expectations.
"I believe we will see BOB trading at $4.5 in the coming few days," the broker said.
Of the four listed industrial firms, Ciments Libanais was flat at $1.28125. There was no trade in tilemaker Uniceramic, pipemaker Eternit or Ciments Blancs.
